description:
## What

Delete `OctoPi.Agent.MessageLog`. Replace `loop.messages :: MessageLog.t()` with `loop.messages :: [AgentMessage]` (a plain list).

Conversions at callsites (~69):

- `MessageLog.new(list)` → `list`
- `MessageLog.push(log, msg)` → `[msg | rev]` style maintained internally, OR just `log ++ [msg]` if simplicity wins (transcripts are dozens of messages, not thousands)
- `MessageLog.append_many(log, msgs)` → `log ++ msgs`
- `MessageLog.to_list(log)` → identity (or `Enum.reverse` if we keep reverse-internal)
- `MessageLog.count(log)` → `length(log)`
- `MessageLog.pop(log)` → `tl(log)` or `List.delete_at(log, -1)` depending on direction
- `MessageLog.find_last_value(log, fun)` → `Enum.find_value(Enum.reverse(log), fun)` or rewrite the call site

Pick a single representation (forward-list vs. reverse-list) and stick to it. Forward-list is simpler; benchmark only if a tight read path objects.

## Why

77-line wrapper around a list with a `count` cache. With Agent's transcript becoming a plain `[AgentMessage]` and synthetic types living in the union, the abstraction obscures more than it earns. Inlining shrinks the surface and removes a layer that has to evolve with every new message type.

## Files

- `apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent/message_log.ex` — deleted.
- `apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent/loop.ex` — call sites rewritten.
- `apps/octo_pi_agent/lib/octo_pi/agent/loop/state.ex` — type rewritten.
- Wherever else MessageLog is referenced (small handful).

## Independent of opi-y0a.1 through opi-y0a.5

Can land first (cosmetic, low risk), last (after the architecture stabilizes), or anywhere in between. No semantic dependency on the other tickets.

## Done when

- `OctoPi.Agent.MessageLog` module is deleted.
- `git grep MessageLog apps/octo_pi_agent` returns empty.
- All existing tests pass.
title: Inline MessageLog into a plain list
